question: How do I create a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To create a kMeet meeting: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or from the desktop/mobile app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter a name for your meeting room. 4) Allow access to webcam and microphone. 5) Enter your name or pseudonym. 6) Optionally enable participant control, password, or encryption. 7) Click 'Join the meeting'. 8) Share the room link to invite participants.
actual_response:
Here is a complete guide to creating a **kMeet meeting**, including prerequisites, platform limitations, and step-by-step instructions:

---

### **How to Create a kMeet Meeting**
#### **Prerequisites**
- No Infomaniak account is required to **create or join** a meeting.
- To **record the meeting** or use advanced features (e.g., participant control, password protection), you must:
  - Be the **first to join the meeting** (automatically granted moderator status).
  - Or be **designated as a moderator** by the current moderator.
- For **scheduling meetings via Infomaniak Calendar**, you need:
  - A **my kSuite** account (e.g., `yourname@ikmail.com`).
  - Access to the [Infomaniak Calendar](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/calendar).

#### **Platform Limitations**
- **Mobile apps** (iOS/Android) and **desktop apps** (Windows/macOS) support all features, including:
  - Participant control.
  - Recording (if you have a kDrive).
  - Live streaming.
- **Web browsers** (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) support all features, but:
  - Some features (e.g., screen sharing) may require **browser permissions**.
  - **Encrypted meetings with a custom key** cannot be recorded.

#### **Technical Specifications**
- **Meeting duration**: No strict limit, but **live streaming** stops after **24 hours**.
- **Participants**: Up to **200 participants** per meeting.
- **Recording format**: Saved as an **.mp4 file** on kDrive.
- **Live streaming**: Broadcast in **HD quality** (if bandwidth allows).

#### **User Role Requirements**
- **Moderator**:
  - Must be the **first to join** or be **designated by another moderator**.
  - Can **control participants** (approve/deny entry, remove participants).
  - Can **enable recording** (if prerequisites are met).
  - Can **start live streaming**.
- **Participants**:
  - Can join via a **link or meeting code**.
  - Can enable/disable their **microphone, camera, and screen sharing**.

#### **Important Warnings/Notes**
- **Encrypted meetings** (with a custom key) **cannot be recorded**.
- **Recordings** are saved to kDrive **only after the meeting ends** (all participants leave).
- **Live streaming** stops when the meeting ends.
- **Guests** (non-Infomaniak users) can join but may have **limited permissions** (e.g., no moderator rights).

#### **Default Behaviors**
- A **unique meeting link** is generated for each session.
- The **General channel** (if using kChat integration) may display the meeting link.
- **No password** is required by default (but can be added manually).

#### **Related Actions**
- **Modify meeting settings**:
  - Add a **password** or **encryption key** before or during the meeting.
  - Enable/disable **participant control** (waiting room).
- **End the meeting**:
  - Close the browser/app window or click **"End meeting for all"** (moderator only).
- **Recordings**:
  - Can be **downloaded, shared, or deleted** from kDrive.
- **Live streaming**:
  - Can be **stopped manually** or automatically after 24 hours.

---

### **How to Create a kMeet Meeting**
#### **Method 1: Quick Start (No Account Required)**
1. Go to **[kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com/)**.
2. Click **"Start a new meeting"**.
3. Enter a **meeting name** (e.g., "Team Sync").
4. Click **"Continue"**.
5. Grant **camera and microphone permissions** when prompted.
6. Enter your **name** (visible to participants).
7. (Optional) Enable **participant control**, add a **password**, or set an **encryption key**.
8. Click **"Join the meeting"**.
9. **Share the meeting link** with participants (click the **user icon with a "+** to copy the link).

---

#### **Method 2: Schedule via Infomaniak Calendar (Requires my kSuite)**
1. Go to **[ksuite.infomaniak.com/calendar](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/calendar)**.
2. Click **"Create"** > **"Event"**.
3. Fill in the **event details** (title, date, time, participants).
4. Click the **green kMeet button** to add a meeting link.
5. Click **"Save"** to send invitations to participants.
6. Participants will receive an **email with the kMeet link**.

---

#### **Method 3: Start from kChat (Team Collaboration)**
1. Open **kChat** (via [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat)).
2. Navigate to a **channel or direct message**.
3. Type **`/kmeet`** and press **Enter**.
4. A **kMeet link** will be generated in the chat.
5. Click the link to **start the meeting**.

---

### **How to Use Advanced Features**
#### **Enable Participant Control (Waiting Room)**
1. Before joining the meeting, click the **chevron (▼)** below the meeting name.
2. Toggle **"Participant control"** to **ON**.
3. Start the meeting.
4. **Approve or deny** participants as they join.

#### **Add a Password or Encryption Key**
1. Before joining, click the **chevron (▼)** below the meeting name.
2. Enter a **password** or **encryption key**.
3. Share the **password/key** with participants separately.

#### **Record the Meeting**
1. **Prerequisites**:
   - You must be a **moderator**.
   - You must have a **kDrive**.
   - The meeting **cannot be encrypted with a custom key**.
2. During the meeting, click the **○○○ menu** in the toolbar.
3. Select **"Start recording"**.
4. Choose a **kDrive** to save the recording.
5. Click **"Start"**.
6. To stop recording, click the **○○○ menu** > **"Stop recording"**.
7. The recording will appear in your kDrive **after the meeting ends**.

#### **Start Live Streaming**
1. **Prerequisites**:
   - You must be a **moderator**.
2. During the meeting, click the **○○○ menu** in the toolbar.
3. Select **"Start live broadcast"**.
4. Click **"Start"**.
5. Copy the **live stream link** and share it with viewers.
6. The stream will **stop automatically after 24 hours** or when the meeting ends.

question: How can I share my screen during a kMeet call?
ground_truth: To share your screen in kMeet: 1) Have the desktop app (macOS/Windows) or mobile app (Android) - screen sharing is not yet available on iOS. 2) Create or join a meeting. 3) Click on the screen icon with an arrow to 'Share your screen'. 4) Validate authorization to access screen content. 5) Choose to share the entire screen or a specific window. 6) Click button to start sharing. 7) To stop, click the toolbar icon again. Note: Permissions may require a restart on first use.

actual_response:
Here’s how you can share your screen during a **kMeet** call, along with important details and limitations:

---

### **How to Share Your Screen on kMeet**
#### **Prerequisites**
- You must be in an active **kMeet meeting** (created or joined).
- Screen sharing is available on:
  - **Desktop apps** (macOS, Windows, Linux).
  - **Web app** (via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) in browsers like Chrome or Firefox).
  - **Mobile apps** (Android only).
    **⚠️ Not available on iOS (iPhone/iPad).**
- If it’s your first time, your device or browser may request **permission** to share the screen. You may need to **restart** the app or browser after granting permissions.

---

#### **Steps to Share Your Screen**
1. **Join or create a meeting** in kMeet:
   - Via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or the desktop/mobile app.
2. **Click the "Share your screen"** icon (looks like a screen with an arrow) in the meeting toolbar.
3. **Choose what to share**:
   - **Entire screen**: Shares everything on your display.
   - **Application window**: Shares only a specific app (e.g., browser, document).
     **⚠️ Note**: If you want participants to **draw on your screen**, you **must** share the **entire screen** (not just a window).
4. **Confirm permissions**:
   - Your device or browser may show a warning. Approve the request to proceed.
5. **Start sharing**:
   - Click the button to begin sharing your screen.
6. **Stop sharing**:
   - Click the same icon again to stop.

---

#### **Platform Limitations**
- **Not available on iOS** (iPhone/iPad).
- **Mobile apps (Android)**:
  - Limited to sharing the **entire screen** (no option to share a specific app window).
- **Web app**:
  - May require additional permissions for first-time use.
- **Desktop apps (macOS/Windows/Linux)**:
  - Full functionality, including screen or window sharing.

---

#### **Important Notes**
- **Permissions**: If the screen-sharing button is grayed out, check your **device/browser permissions** for screen recording:
  - **macOS**: Go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording** and enable kMeet or your browser.
  - **Windows**: Ensure kMeet has permission to access your screen in **Settings > Privacy > Screen Recording**.
- **Collaboration features**:
  - If you share your **entire screen**, participants can **draw on it** or **request remote control** (if enabled).
  - If you share only an **app window**, drawing and remote control are **disabled**.
- **Performance**: Sharing high-resolution screens (e.g., 4K) may impact performance. Close unnecessary apps for smoother sharing.

---
#### **Related Actions**
- **Draw on a shared screen**: Participants can annotate your shared screen if you share the **entire screen**. They’ll see a pencil icon in the toolbar.
- **Remote control**: Participants can request to **control your device** if you share the entire screen. You’ll need to approve the request.
- **Stop sharing**: Click the screen-sharing icon again to stop.

---
#### **Troubleshooting**
- If screen sharing fails:
  - Restart the kMeet app or browser.
  - Check **device/browser permissions** (see above).
  - Ensure no other app is using screen recording (e.g., OBS, Zoom).
  - Try a different browser (Chrome or Firefox recommended for the web app).

---

- [Solving problems on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/289/solving-a-problem-on-kmeet)

question: What should I do if my audio is not working in kMeet?
ground_truth: To fix audio issues in kMeet: 1) Go to kMeet Settings and reauthorize microphone access. 2) Check browser lock icon isn't blocking multimedia. 3) On mobile, check Settings > Privacy > Microphone permissions for kMeet. 4) On Windows, use Privacy settings and Audio Troubleshooter. 5) Try joining from a different device (mobile instead of computer or vice versa). 6) As last resort on Firefox, disable WebRTC in about:config by setting media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
actual_response:
If your audio is not working in **kMeet**, follow these troubleshooting steps:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- You must have a **microphone** connected to your device (built-in or external).
- You must have granted **microphone permissions** to kMeet in your browser or desktop app.
- You must be using a **supported browser** (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) or the **kMeet desktop/mobile app**.

---

### **Troubleshooting Steps**

#### **1. Check Microphone Permissions**
- **For browsers (Web version):**
  - Click the **lock icon** 🔒 in the address bar.
  - Ensure **microphone access** is allowed for kMeet.
  - If blocked, enable it and **reload** the page.

- **For kMeet desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux):**
  - Open **kMeet Settings** (click the ⚙️ icon at the top right).
  - Go to the **Audio** section.
  - Select the correct microphone from the dropdown menu.
  - Ensure the microphone is **not muted** (check for a crossed-out microphone icon).

- **For mobile (iOS/Android):**
  - Open your device’s **Settings**.
  - Go to **Apps** > **kMeet** > **Permissions**.
  - Enable **Microphone** access.

---

#### **2. Test Your Microphone**
- **On Windows:**
  - Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Sound**.
  - Under **Input**, check if your microphone is detected and working.
  - Use the **Troubleshoot** button if needed.

- **On macOS:**
  - Go to **System Settings** > **Sound** > **Input**.
  - Select your microphone and check the input level.

- **On Mobile (iOS/Android):**
  - Open a voice recording app (e.g., Voice Memos) to test if the microphone works.

---

#### **3. Restart kMeet and Your Device**
- **Close kMeet completely** (quit the app or close the browser tab).
- **Restart your device** (computer, phone, or tablet).
- Reopen kMeet and **rejoin the meeting**.

---

#### **4. Switch Devices or Browsers**
- If audio still doesn’t work, **join the meeting from another device** (e.g., switch from computer to phone).
- If using a **browser**, try switching to **Chrome, Firefox, or Edge**.
- If using the **kMeet app**, try the **web version** (or vice versa).

---

#### **5. Check for Firewall or Network Restrictions**
- A **firewall** or **corporate network** may block kMeet’s audio.
- **Allow the following in your firewall settings:**
  - **UDP Protocol:** `443`
  - **TCP Port:** `443` (for *turn server*)
  - **IP Addresses:** `185.125.24.0/24` (TCP and UDP)
- If possible, **switch from WiFi to mobile data (4G/5G)** to test if the issue is network-related.

---

#### **6. Update kMeet and Your Browser/App**
- **For the kMeet app:**
  - Check for updates in your app store (Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android).
- **For browsers:**
  - Update your browser to the latest version.

---

#### **7. Check for Muted Participants**
- If **other participants** can’t hear you:
  - Ensure you are **not muted** in kMeet (check the microphone icon in the meeting).
  - Ask the **meeting host** to check if you are muted by them.
- If **you can’t hear others:**
  - Check if your **speaker/headphone volume** is turned up.
  - Ensure you are **not muted** in kMeet.

---

#### **8. Rejoin the Meeting**
- **Leave the meeting** and rejoin using the same link.
- If possible, **generate a new meeting link** and try again.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- **No known platform-specific limitations** for audio in kMeet (works on **Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and web browsers**).
- However, **some corporate networks or firewalls** may block audio streams.

---

### **User Role Requirements**
- **All participants** (including guests) can troubleshoot their own audio issues.
- **Moderators/hosts** can mute/unmute participants but cannot fix individual audio issues.

---

### **Important Warnings**
- If you are on **"Do Not Disturb"** mode in **kChat**, calls may not ring, but you can still join manually.
- If the meeting is **recorded**, audio issues may affect the recording quality.
- **Guests** (non-Infomaniak users) may have limited permissions but can still troubleshoot their own audio.

---

### **Default Behaviors**
- The **microphone is enabled by default** when you join a meeting (but you may need to allow permissions).
- The **camera is disabled by default** (but the microphone is not).

---

### **Related Actions**
- **Disable/Enable Microphone:** Click the microphone icon in kMeet.
- **Switch Microphone:** Go to **Settings** > **Audio** and select a different device.
- **Leave and Rejoin:** Exit the meeting and rejoin if audio cuts out.

---

### **If the Issue Persists**
- Contact **[Infomaniak Support](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support)** for further assistance.
- Provide details about:
  - Your **device** (computer/phone/tablet).
  - Your **operating system** (Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android).
  - Your **browser/app version** (if applicable).
  - Whether the issue affects **all participants** or just you.

---
**Sources:**
- [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)
- [Solving a problem on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/289/solving-a-problem-on-kmeet)

question: How do I create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet?
ground_truth: To create side rooms in kMeet: 1) You must be a moderator. 2) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 3) Once participants are in the meeting, click on the multi-user icon in the toolbar. 4) Click the button to add a side room. 5) Participants can then join or leave the room. 6) The moderator can force participants to join a specific side room via the action menu. Side rooms allow dividing a main meeting into several simultaneous discussions in distinct virtual spaces.
key_points: moderator can force participants to join
actual_response:
Here’s how to create **side rooms (breakout rooms)** in kMeet:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- You **must be a moderator** of the kMeet meeting. Only moderators can create and manage side rooms.
- Participants can join side rooms but cannot create them.
- Side rooms are available on **all platforms** (Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android).

---

### **How to Create Side Rooms (Breakout Rooms)**
1. **Start a kMeet meeting** as a moderator:
   - Go to [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or open the kMeet app on your device.
   - Create or join a meeting and ensure you have **moderator rights**.

2. **Access the side rooms feature**:
   - Once the meeting has started, click on the **multi-user icon** (looks like a group of people) in the kMeet toolbar.

3. **Add a side room**:
   - Click the **button to add a side room** (e.g., "Add a side room" or "+").
   - A new side room will appear in the list.

4. **Manage participants**:
   - **Option 1**: Participants can **join the side room voluntarily** by clicking on the side room name in the list.
   - **Option 2**: As a moderator, you can **force a participant to join a side room**:
     - Click on the **action menu (three dots)** next to the participant’s name in the participant list.
     - Select **Move to side room** and choose the desired side room.

5. **Switch between rooms**:
   - Moderators can move between the **main room** and **side rooms** at any time.
   - Participants can leave a side room to return to the main room by clicking the **multi-user icon** and selecting the main room.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- Side rooms are **available on all platforms** (Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android).
- No known limitations for side rooms on specific platforms.

---

### **User Role Requirements**
- **Moderators**: Can create, manage, and close side rooms. They can also move participants between rooms.
- **Participants**: Can join side rooms but cannot create or manage them.

---

### **Important Warnings or Notes**
- Side rooms **stop when the main meeting ends**. All participants are automatically returned to the main room before the meeting closes.
- Moderators can **close side rooms manually** at any time.
- Side rooms are **not recorded** even if the main meeting is being recorded. Only the main room is recorded.

---

### **Related Actions**
- **Close a side room**: As a moderator, click the **multi-user icon** and select the side room to close it.
- **Rename a side room**: Currently, side rooms are named numerically (e.g., "Side Room 1"). Renaming is not supported yet.
- **Delete a side room**: Close the side room, and it will disappear from the list.

---
### **How to Use Side Rooms Effectively**
- Use side rooms for **group discussions**, workshops, or team collaborations during a larger meeting.
- Assign a **moderator or facilitator** to each side room if needed.
- Communicate clearly with participants about when and how to join side rooms.

---
**Source**: [Infomaniak Support - Create a kMeet Meeting Side Room](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room)

question: How can I record a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To record a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Have a kDrive, be the moderator, and don't use encrypted meeting with custom key. Steps: 1) Start kMeet. 2) Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (three dots). 3) Click 'Start recording'. 4) Log in to Infomaniak if needed and select a kDrive for storage. 5) To stop, click the toolbar again and choose 'Stop recording'. 6) The recording is saved to the kDrive root in .mp4 format when all participants leave. Maximum duration is 3 hours.
actual_response:
Here’s how you can record a **kMeet meeting**, along with all relevant details from the documentation:

---

### **How to Record a kMeet Meeting**
#### **Prerequisites**
- You **must have a kDrive** (standalone or as part of a kSuite/my kSuite).
- You **must be the moderator** of the video conference.
- The meeting **must not be encrypted with a custom key** (recording is not supported in this case).

---

#### **Platform Limitations**
- Recording is **available on all platforms** (Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android).
- The recording is saved **directly to kDrive** (not locally on your device).

---

#### **Technical Specifications**
- **File format**: `.mp4`.
- **Maximum duration**: **3 hours** per recording.
- Recording is done **server-side**, so it does not consume your device’s resources.

---

#### **User Role Requirements**
- **Only the moderator** can start and stop the recording.

---

#### **Important Warnings/Notes**
- The recording is **only available after the meeting ends** (i.e., when all participants have left the virtual room).
- If the meeting is encrypted with a custom key, **recording is not possible**.
- Participants are **not explicitly notified** when recording starts or stops (though a red "Recording" indicator appears in the meeting).

---

#### **Steps to Record a kMeet Meeting**
1. **Start kMeet**:
   - Open [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or use the **desktop/mobile app**.
   - Create or join a meeting as the **moderator**.

2. **Start Recording**:
   - Click the **action menu (○○○)** in the kMeet toolbar.
   - Select **Start recording (◉)**.
   - Log in to your Infomaniak account if prompted.
   - Choose the **kDrive** where the recording will be saved.
   - Click **Start** to begin recording.

3. **Stop Recording**:
   - Click the **action menu (○○○)** again.
   - Select **Stop recording**.
   - Confirm the action.
   - Choose whether to **go to the recording location on kDrive**.

4. **Access the Recording**:
   - The recording is saved at the **root of your selected kDrive**.
   - It becomes available **after the meeting ends** (when all participants have left).

---

#### **Default Behavior**
- The recording is **automatically saved to kDrive** in `.mp4` format.
- The file is named with the **meeting name and timestamp**.

---

#### **Related Actions**
- **Delete the recording**: Manually delete the `.mp4` file from kDrive.
- **Share the recording**: Use kDrive’s sharing options to share the file with others.
- **Disable recording**: If you no longer want to record, simply do not start the recording or stop it manually.

---
#### **How to Use the Recording**
- Play the `.mp4` file using any video player (e.g., VLC, QuickTime).
- Share the file via kDrive’s sharing features (e.g., public link, email invitation).

---
### **Sources**

question: How do I set a password for my kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To protect a kMeet meeting with a password: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter the meeting room name. 4) Click on 'security options'. 5) Enable the toggle switch to 'Protect access'. 6) Create the password. 7) Click Continue to start. 8) Share both the meeting link/code AND the password with participants. You can also enable end-to-end encryption from security options (works only with Chromium-based browsers).
actual_response:
Here’s how to set a password for your **kMeet meeting**:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- You must be the **meeting organizer** or **moderator** (the first person to start the meeting).
- The password must be shared with participants so they can join.
- Password protection can be enabled **during meeting creation** or **before participants join**.

---

### **Steps to Set a Password for a kMeet Meeting**
1. **Start kMeet**:
   - Go to **[kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com/)** or open the kMeet app on your computer or mobile device.

2. **Create a new meeting**:
   - Click **Start a new meeting**.

3. **Configure the meeting**:
   - Enter a **name** for your meeting room.
   - Click on the **security options** (or the shield icon).

4. **Enable password protection**:
   - Toggle the switch to **Protect access**.
   - Enter a **password** of your choice.

5. **Start the meeting**:
   - Click **Continue** or **Start** to begin the meeting.

6. **Share the meeting details**:
   - Enter your **name** as a participant.
   - Copy the **meeting link or code** and **password**.
   - Share these details with your participants (via email, chat, etc.).

7. **Manage participants (optional)**:
   - If you enabled **participant control**, you can approve or deny entry to participants from the waiting room.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- Password protection is available on **all platforms** (web, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android).
- Participants must enter the password **before joining** the meeting.

---

### **Important Notes**
- The password is **required for all participants** to join the meeting.
- If you enable **participant control**, you must manually approve participants even if they have the password.
- The password can be **re-displayed** during the meeting if needed (click the **invite participants** button).

---

### **How Participants Join with a Password**
1. Participants click the **meeting link** or enter the **meeting code** on [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com/).
2. They enter the **password** provided by the organizer.
3. They join the meeting once the password is validated.

---
### **Related Actions**
- **Change the password**: Disable and re-enable the password protection in the security settings.
- **Remove the password**: Toggle off the **Protect access** option during the meeting.
- **Enable encryption key**: For additional security, you can also set a **custom encryption key** (see [this guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2464)).

---

- [Create a kMeet meeting](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2475)
- [Join a kMeet meeting](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2473)

Here’s how to **livestream a kMeet meeting** using the **Live Streaming mode**:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- You **must be a moderator** of the kMeet meeting to start a livestream.
- You **do not need** an Infomaniak Video Streaming subscription to create a livestream link.
- The livestream is accessible via a **unique URL** and can be viewed by an **unlimited number of participants**.
- The livestream **stops automatically** when the kMeet meeting ends.
- The maximum duration of the livestream is **24 hours**.

Here’s how to resolve sync conflicts in **kDrive**, based on the official documentation:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- You must have the **kDrive desktop app** installed (macOS, Windows, or Linux).
- Conflicts typically occur when the **same file is modified simultaneously** on multiple devices or on **kDrive Web** while the app is offline.
- Conflicts are **not automatically resolved** for all cases; manual intervention may be required.

---

### **How Sync Conflicts Occur**
Conflicts arise in the following scenarios:
- A file is modified **locally** and **on kDrive Web** at the same time.
- A file is **created or moved** while a similar operation occurs simultaneously on kDrive Web.
- A file is modified **locally**, but its parent folder was deleted on kDrive Web.
- A file move **cannot be synchronized correctly**.

---

### **How kDrive Handles Conflicts**
- The **kDrive Web version** is always prioritized.
- The **local version** is saved with the suffix `_conflict` (e.g., `document_conflict.docx`).
- The conflicting file (**`_conflict`**) is **not synchronized** with kDrive Web.

---

### **How to Resolve Sync Conflicts**
#### **Step 1: Identify Conflicts**
1. Click the **kDrive desktop app icon** in your computer’s notification area:
   - **macOS**: Top-right corner.
   - **Windows**: Bottom-right corner (double-click in the taskbar on Linux).
2. Click the **information (i) button** at the top.
3. Go to the **Conflicts tab** to view unsynchronized files.

#### **Step 2: Resolve the Conflict**
You have **three options** to resolve the conflict:

##### **Option 1: Keep Both Versions (Manual Merge)**
1. Open both files:
   - The **original file** (prioritized by kDrive Web).
   - The **`_conflict` file** (your local version).
2. **Compare** the differences between the two files.
3. **Manually merge** the changes from the `_conflict` file into the original file.
4. **Delete** the `_conflict` file after merging.

##### **Option 2: Keep the Original File (Discard Local Changes)**
- If the **original file** (kDrive Web version) is up to date:
  1. **Delete** the `_conflict` file.
  2. The original file will remain synchronized.

##### **Option 3: Keep the Conflict File (Discard kDrive Web Version)**
- If the **`_conflict` file** contains the correct version:
  1. **Delete** the original file.
  2. **Rename** the `_conflict` file by removing the `_conflict` suffix (e.g., `document.docx`).
  3. The renamed file will now synchronize with kDrive Web.

---

### **Special Cases**
#### **For kDrive App Versions Prior to 3.6.11**
- The **kDrive Web version** is always prioritized.
- Local files are renamed with `_conflict`.
- If a file was deleted on kDrive Web but modified locally, the local file is **kept and resynchronized**.

#### **For kDrive App Version 3.6.11 and Later**
- For **Lite Sync "placeholder" files** (dehydrated files):
  - Conflicting files are **automatically deleted locally**.
  - If the file still exists on kDrive Web, it is **resynchronized**.
- For **other conflicts**:
  - The **kDrive Web version** is prioritized.
  - Local files are renamed with `_conflict`.
  - If a locally modified file should be deleted (based on kDrive Web), it is **moved to a "kDrive Rescue Folder"** instead of being deleted.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- **Lite Sync** is available on **macOS and Windows** but **not on Linux**.
- Conflicts involving **dehydrated files** (Lite Sync) require manual intervention to download the full file from kDrive Web.
- Conflicts are **not visible on mobile devices** (Android/iOS); they must be resolved on a desktop.

---

### **Important Warnings**
- **Do not work on the same file simultaneously** with multiple people unless using **online collaboration** (e.g., Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files).
- **Synchronize offline modifications** before editing the same files online.
- **Avoid creating folders with the same name** as unsynchronized folders.
- **Conflicts are not resolved automatically** for all cases; manual review is often required.
- **Files with `_conflict` are not synchronized** until resolved.

---

### **How to Avoid Future Conflicts**
- **Enable Lite Sync** (if storage space is limited) to reduce the risk of conflicts with dehydrated files.
- **Check the kDrive app icon** regularly for synchronization status (orange = conflict, green = synchronized).
- **Avoid modifying files offline** for extended periods.
- **Use the kDrive Web app** for collaborative editing when possible.

- **Restore a deleted file**: [See guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2383).

   ![Manage users](https://faq.storage5.infomaniak.com/34dab26b093e259d77f0b6e623e3c033deb67c42.gif)

---
---

### **2. Modify a User’s Permissions**
#### **User Role Requirements:**
- You must be an **Administrator** of the kDrive or the **Organization**.
- If you cannot modify permissions, you may need to adjust the user’s **Organization-level role** first (e.g., demote them from **Administrator** to **User**).

#### **Steps:**
1. In the **Manage users** section, locate the user whose rights you want to modify.
2. Click the **action menu (⋮)** next to their name.
3. Select **Edit permissions**.
4. Choose one of the following access levels:
   - **Administrator**:
     - Full control over kDrive (sharing, statistics, activity reports, restoring/deleting folders, importing data, etc.).
     - Access to all files and folders.
   - **User**:
     - Access to shared files and folders.
     - Can create, modify, and share their own files/folders.
     - **Cannot** manage kDrive settings (e.g., add/remove users, view statistics, or delete root folders).
5. Click **Save**.

#### **Important Notes:**
- Users with **User** rights cannot create folders at the root of **Organization Folders**.
- Users with **Administrator** rights can manage all aspects of kDrive, including user invitations and deletions.

---
---

### **3. Advanced User Actions**
#### **User Role Requirements:**
- You must be an **Administrator** or **kDrive Solo owner** to perform these actions.

#### **Available Actions:**
1. **Block a User**:
   - Temporarily revoke access without deleting their account.
   - Steps:
     1. Go to **Manage users**.
     2. Click the **action menu (⋮)** next to the user.
     3. Select **Block user**.

2. **Remove a User from kDrive**:
   - Permanently delete the user from kDrive.
   - Steps:
     1. Go to **Manage users**.
     2. Click the **action menu (⋮)** next to the user.
     3. Select **Remove from kDrive**.
     4. Confirm the action.

3. **Replace the kDrive Solo User**:
   - Transfer ownership of a **kDrive Solo** to another user in the Organization.
   - Steps:
     1. Go to **Dashboard** > **Manage users**.
     2. Click the **action menu (⋮)** next to the current user.
     3. Select **Replace user**.
     4. Choose the new user from the Organization.
     5. Decide whether to **retain or delete** existing data.
     6. Click **Replace**.

4. **View User Activity**:
   - Check a user’s actions (e.g., file modifications, shares).
   - Steps:
     1. Go to **Manage users**.
     2. Click the **action menu (⋮)** next to the user.
     3. Select **View activity**.

---
---

### **4. Invite a New User to kDrive**
#### **User Role Requirements:**
- You must be an **Administrator** or **User with sharing permissions**.

#### **Steps:**
1. Go to **Manage users**.
2. Click **Invite a new user**.
3. Choose one of the following:
   - **Add a user to the Drive**: Select an existing **Organization user**.
   - **Add a user to my Organization**: Invite an external user via email.
4. Enter the user’s email address.
5. Assign their permissions (**Administrator** or **User**).
6. Click **Invite**.
   - The user will receive an email invitation (valid for **1 month**).

#### **Important Notes:**
- External users (not part of the Organization) have **limited permissions** (e.g., cannot access Organization-wide shares).
- Users invited to **kSuite** automatically gain access to kDrive if it’s part of the suite.

---
---

### **5. Manage Folder-Level Permissions**
#### **User Role Requirements:**
- You must be an **Administrator** or the **owner of the folder**.

#### **Steps:**
1. Right-click the folder you want to share.
2. Select **Share**.
3. Choose the user or group from the list or enter their email address.
4. Assign one of the following permissions:
   - **View**: Read-only access (download, comment).
   - **Modify**: Edit, download, comment, add/delete files.
   - **Manage**: Full control (share with others, manage rights).
5. Click **Save**.

#### **Important Notes:**
- Permissions can be **restricted** for specific folders (e.g., a subfolder can have different permissions than its parent).
- Public links (green icon) are visible in the **"Who has access"** column.

---
---

### **6. Organization-Level Permissions**
#### **Prerequisites:**
- You must be an **Organization Administrator** or **Legal Representative**.

#### **Steps:**
1. Go to the [Infomaniak Manager](https://manager.infomaniak.com).
2. Select your **Organization**.
3. Navigate to **Users** > **Product Access**.
4. Locate the user and click their name.
5. Under **kDrive**, assign one of the following:
   - **Technical Rights**: Manage kDrive settings (e.g., user invitations, storage).
   - **Statistical Rights**: View kDrive usage statistics (e.g., storage, active users).
   - **No Rights**: Only basic access (no management or statistics).

#### **Important Notes:**
- Users with **Technical Rights** can manage kDrive but **cannot** see statistics unless **Statistical Rights** are also enabled.
- Users with **no rights** can still access kDrive if they are invited as a **User** or **Administrator** within kDrive itself.

---
---

### **7. Platform Limitations**
- **Mobile Apps (iOS/Android)**:
  - User management (e.g., inviting users, modifying permissions) is **not available** on mobile apps. Use the **Web app** for these actions.
- **Lite Sync (Desktop)**:
  - Not available on **Linux**.
  - On **Windows/macOS**, Lite Sync does not support **real-time collaboration** (e.g., simultaneous editing).

---
---

### **8. Default Behaviors**
- **Organization Folders**: All users can see the **Organization Folders** directory by default, but sharing can be restricted.
- **Personal Folders**: Users have a **private folder** by default, visible only to them unless shared.
- **General Channel**: Not applicable to kDrive (this is a **kChat** feature).

---
---

### **9. Related Actions**
- **Convert a User to Administrator**: Follow the steps in [Section 2](#2-modify-a-users-permissions).
- **Archive a Folder**: Right-click the folder > **Archive**.
- **Disable Sharing**: Right-click the folder > **Share** > Remove the user.
- **Leave a Shared Folder**: Right-click the folder > **Leave share**.

---
---

### **10. Important Warnings**
- **Data Deletion**: Removing a user from kDrive **does not delete their files**. Their files remain in the kDrive unless manually deleted.
- **External Users**: They cannot access **Organization-wide shares** (e.g., calendars, address books).
- **kDrive Solo**: Only the **Solo administrator** can transfer ownership to another user.
- **Permissions Hierarchy**: Folder-level permissions **override** kDrive-wide permissions (e.g., a user with **User** rights can still be granted **Manage** permissions for a specific folder).

---
---

### **Sources**
- [Manage a kDrive User’s Rights](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365)
- [Understanding kDrive Permissions](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2501)
- [Manage kDrive Users](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2364)
- [Manage Organization User’s Product Access](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1610)

question: How can I access kDrive files locally without downloading them?
ground_truth: To access kDrive files locally: 1) Install the kDrive desktop app. 2) Click on the kDrive icon in notification area (top right macOS, bottom right Windows, double-click on Linux). 3) Click action menu at top right. 4) Choose 'Open kDrive Web' to access server files. 5) Or click the item above to open the local folder. Files can be physically present or virtually present (if Lite Sync is enabled). Lite Sync allows files to appear locally without taking up disk space - they download on demand when opened.
key_points: Open kDrive Web for server files
actual_response:
To access your **kDrive files locally without downloading them entirely**, you can use the **Lite Sync** feature available in the kDrive desktop app (for **Windows** and **macOS**). This allows you to view and access files virtually without occupying full storage space on your device. Here’s how it works:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- Install the **[kDrive desktop app](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2374)** on your **Windows** or **macOS** device.
- Ensure you are logged in to your Infomaniak account.
- Lite Sync is **not available on Linux** or mobile devices (iOS/Android).

---

### **How to Enable Lite Sync**
Lite Sync allows you to:
- View all files and folders in your kDrive locally **without downloading them entirely**.
- Download files **only when you open them**.
- Save storage space on your device.

#### **On Windows**
1. Open the kDrive desktop app.
2. Click on the kDrive icon in the notification area (bottom-right corner).
3. Click the **⋮ (action menu)** and select **Settings**.
4. Go to the **Sync** tab.
5. Enable the **Lite Sync** option for the desired kDrive.
6. Confirm your choice.
   - Files will now appear locally but will only download when accessed.
   - A cloud icon (☁️) indicates files that are not fully downloaded.
   - *Source: [Manage Lite Sync on Windows](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2562/manage-the-lite-sync-kdrive-option-windows)*
.

---

#### **On macOS**
1. Open the kDrive desktop app.
2. Click on the kDrive icon in the menu bar (top-right corner).
3. Click the **⋮ (action menu)** and select **Preferences**.
4. Go to the **Sync** tab.
5. Enable the **Lite Sync** option for the desired kDrive.
6. Confirm your choice.
   - Files will now appear locally but will only download when accessed.
   - A cloud icon (☁️) indicates files that are not fully downloaded.
   - *Source: [Manage Lite Sync on macOS](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2608/manage-the-kdrive-lite-sync-option-macos)*.

---

### **How to Access Files Locally**
1. Open the **kDrive folder** on your computer (created during installation).
   - Files with a **cloud icon (☁️)** are not fully downloaded.
2. **Double-click** a file to download and open it.
   - The file will download automatically when accessed.
3. Once downloaded, the file remains available offline until you manually remove it or disable Lite Sync.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- **Lite Sync is not available on:**
  - **Linux** (only full synchronization is supported).
  - **Mobile devices** (iOS/Android).
- **Web app (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive):** Files are always accessible online, but Lite Sync does not apply here.

---

### **Important Notes**
- Files marked with a **cloud icon (☁️)** are **not fully downloaded** and require an internet connection to open.
- If you **disable Lite Sync**, all files will download to your device, which may take up significant storage space.
- Lite Sync is **kDrive-specific**: If you sync multiple kDrives, you can enable/disable Lite Sync for each one independently.
- *Source: [Access kDrive files locally](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2456/access-kdrive-files-locally-and-online)*
.

---

### **How to Disable Lite Sync**
1. Open the kDrive desktop app.
2. Go to **Settings** (Windows) or **Preferences** (macOS).
3. Navigate to the **Sync** tab.
4. Disable the **Lite Sync** option.
5. Confirm your choice.
   - All files will now download fully to your device.

---

### **Default Behavior**
- The **kDrive folder** is created automatically during installation.
- Files are **virtually accessible** but only download when opened (if Lite Sync is enabled).

---

### **Related Actions**
- **Convert to full sync**: Disable Lite Sync to download all files.
- **Free up space**: Manually remove downloaded files (they remain available online).
- **Check sync status**: Click the kDrive icon in the notification area/menu bar to see sync progress.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

question: How do I sync kDrive with my Synology NAS?
ground_truth: To sync kDrive with Synology NAS via WebDAV: Prerequisites: Synology NAS accessible from Internet, know your kDrive ID. Steps: 1) Log in to Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM). 2) Install Cloud Sync from Package Center if needed. 3) Open Cloud Sync. 4) Click + to add a Cloud. 5) Choose WebDAV. 6) Enter: Server address: https://[kDriveID].connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com, Username: Infomaniak email, Password: create an application password. 7) Select local folder, destination, and sync type: Bidirectional (changes in both directions), Download remote only (backup kDrive to NAS), or Download local only (backup NAS to kDrive).
key_points: Bidirectional, Download remote, or Download local sync
actual_response:
Here’s how to sync **kDrive with your Synology NAS** using the **WebDAV** protocol via the **Cloud Sync** app:

---

### **Prerequisites**
- A **Synology NAS** accessible from the Internet.
- Your **[kDrive identifier (kDrive ID)](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2409)** (e.g., `12345`).
- An **Infomaniak account email address** and an **[application password](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2356)** (do not use your main account password).

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- This method is **only available for Synology NAS** (not applicable to other NAS brands without WebDAV support).
- Requires **Cloud Sync** app installed on the Synology NAS.

---

### **Steps to Sync kDrive with Synology NAS**
1. **Log in to Synology DSM**:
   - Access your Synology NAS administration interface (DSM).

2. **Install Cloud Sync** (if not already installed):
   - Open **Package Center**.
   - Search for **Cloud Sync** and install it.

3. **Open Cloud Sync**:
   - Launch the **Cloud Sync** app from the DSM main menu.

4. **Add a New Cloud Provider**:
   - Click the **+** button at the bottom left to add a new cloud connection.

5. **Select WebDAV**:
   - Scroll to the bottom of the list and select **WebDAV**.

6. **Configure WebDAV Connection**:
   - **Server address**:
     `https://IDkDrive.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com`
     (Replace `IDkDrive` with your actual kDrive ID, e.g., `12345.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com`).
   - **Username**: Your **Infomaniak account email address**.
   - **Password**: Use an **[application password](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2356)** (not your main account password).

7. **Select Sync Settings**:
   - **Local folder**: Choose the folder on your Synology NAS where files will be synced.
   - **Remote folder**: Select the folder in your kDrive to sync.
   - **Sync direction**:
     - **Bidirectional**: Changes on either side (kDrive or NAS) will sync to the other.
     - **Download remote changes only**: Only sync from kDrive to NAS (ideal for backups).
     - **Upload local changes only**: Only sync from NAS to kDrive (ideal for uploading NAS data to kDrive).

8. **Complete Setup**:
   - Click **Next** and review the settings.
   - Click **Apply** to start the synchronization.

---

### **Important Notes**
- **Application Password**: Always use an **[application password](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2356)** for security. Do not use your main Infomaniak account password.
- **Sync Frequency**: Cloud Sync will run continuously or at intervals (configurable in the task settings).
- **File Size Limits**: kDrive supports files up to **5 TB** in size, but large files may slow down syncing.
- **Supported File Types**: All file types are supported, but some may require specific apps to open (e.g., `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.mp4`).
- **Conflict Handling**: If the same file is modified on both kDrive and the NAS, Cloud Sync will create a duplicate to avoid data loss.

---

### **Troubleshooting**
- If the connection fails, verify:
  - The **kDrive ID** is correct.
  - The **application password** is valid.
  - Your **Synology NAS has internet access**.
  - The **WebDAV service is enabled** on kDrive (it is enabled by default).
- For further assistance, contact [Infomaniak Support](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support).

---
### **Related Actions**
- **Modify Sync Settings**: Open Cloud Sync, select the task, and click **Edit**.
- **Pause Sync**: Select the task and click **Pause**.
- **Delete Sync Task**: Select the task and click **Delete**.

---
**Source**: [Sync Synology with kDrive](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2404/sync-synology-with-kdrive)

question: How do I create a channel in kChat?

To convert public to private: click channel > chevron > Convert (permanent). To leave: chevron > Leave. To archive: chevron > Archive. Can also add to favorites, mute, or organize by categories.

Here’s how to create a channel in **kChat**, along with important details:

---

### **How to Create a Channel in kChat**
#### **Prerequisites**
- You must be a member of a **kChat Organization** (part of kSuite).
- No specific role is required to create a **public channel**, but you must be invited to create or join a **private channel**.

#### **Steps to Create a Channel**
1. **Access kChat**:

question: What slash commands are available in kChat?
ground_truth: To use slash commands in kChat: 1) Click in the composition field. 2) Type / followed by the command. 3) Send. Typing just / shows available commands in a modal (like going offline). You can create custom slash commands: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Click 'Slash command'. 5) Add a command with name, trigger, content type, and action. Custom commands can call external APIs or run scripts. Note: External users cannot see the Integrations menu.
actual_response:
Here are the **slash commands** available in **kChat**, along with their functionalities, prerequisites, and limitations:

---

### **Default Slash Commands in kChat**
To use a slash command:
1. Open a channel or direct message in kChat.
2. Type `/` in the message composition field.
3. Select a command from the list or type it manually (e.g., `/away`).
4. Press **Enter** to execute the command.

---

#### **List of Default Slash Commands**
| Command               | Description                                                                                     | Prerequisites / Notes                                                                                     |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `/away`               | Set your status to "Away."                                                                      | Available to all users.                                                                                   |
| `/online`             | Set your status to "Online."                                                                    | Available to all users.                                                                                   |
| `/offline`            | Set your status to "Offline."                                                                   | Available to all users.                                                                                   |
| `/dnd`                | Set your status to "Do Not Disturb."                                                            | Available to all users. Notifications are muted.                                                          |
| `/clear`              | Clear the current channel's messages from your view.                                            | Does not delete messages for other users. Available to all users.                                         |
| `/help`               | Display the list of available slash commands.                                                   | Available to all users.                                                                                    |
| `/invite @user`       | Invite a user to the current channel.                                                           | Must have permission to invite users to the channel.                                                      |
| `/leave`              | Leave the current channel.                                                                      | Cannot leave the **General** channel (default channel).                                                   |
| `/mute`               | Mute the current channel.                                                                       | Available to all users.                                                                                    |
| `/unmute`             | Unmute the current channel.                                                                     | Available to all users.                                                                                    |
| `/rename [new name]`  | Rename the current channel.                                                                     | Must be a **channel administrator** or **organization administrator**.                                    |
| `/search [keyword]`   | Search for messages containing a specific keyword.                                              | Available to all users.                                                                                    |
| `/settings`           | Open your personal settings.                                                                    | Available to all users.                                                                                    |
| `/shortcuts`          | Display keyboard shortcuts.                                                                     | Available to all users.                                                                                    |

---

### **Custom Slash Commands**
You can also **create custom slash commands** to integrate with external services or automate tasks.

#### **Prerequisites for Custom Slash Commands**
- You must **not** be an **external user** (guests cannot create integrations).
- You need access to the **Integrations** menu in kChat.
- For advanced commands (e.g., calling an API), you may need **programming skills** or an external script.

#### **How to Create a Custom Slash Command**
1. Open the **kChat Web app** ([ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat)) or the **desktop app**.
2. Click the **New** icon (➕) next to your organization's name.
3. Select **Integrations**.
4. Click **Slash command**.
5. Click **Add a command**.
6. Configure the command:
   - **Name**: The command users will type (e.g., `/weather`).
   - **Trigger**: The word that follows `/` (e.g., `weather`).
   - **Description**: Explain what the command does.
   - **Response type**: Choose how kChat responds (e.g., in-channel message, ephemeral message).
   - **URL** (optional): If the command calls an external API, enter the endpoint.
   - **Autocomplete**: Enable if you want the command to appear in the suggestions list.
7. **Save** the command.
8. Test the command in a channel.

#### **Limitations of Custom Slash Commands**
- Custom commands **do not appear** in the `/help` list by default.
- External users (guests) **cannot use restricted commands** (e.g., `/invite`, `/rename`).
- Advanced integrations (e.g., API calls) require **external hosting** for scripts.

---

### **Platform Limitations**
- **Mobile apps (iOS/Android)**:
  - Some commands (e.g., `/settings`) may redirect you to the **web app** for full functionality.
  - Custom slash commands work, but **autocomplete** may be limited.
- **Desktop apps (Windows/macOS/Linux)**:
  - Full support for all slash commands.
  - Custom commands work seamlessly.

---

### **Important Notes**
- **Guests** (external users) have **limited access** to slash commands. They cannot:
  - Use restricted commands like `/invite`, `/rename`, or `/leave` for channels they don’t own.
  - Create or modify custom slash commands.
- **Default channels** (e.g., **General**) cannot be left or archived.
- **Slash commands are case-insensitive** (e.g., `/Away` and `/away` work the same way).

---

### **Related Actions**
- **Disable a custom command**: Go to **Integrations** > **Slash commands** > Select the command > **Delete**.
- **Modify a custom command**: Go to **Integrations** > **Slash commands** > Select the command > Edit settings.
- **View all commands**: Type `/` in any channel to see the list.

---

- [Invite an External User to kChat](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat)

4. Click **Save**.

#### **Prerequisites**

### **What is Euria?**
Euria is an **artificial intelligence (AI)** integrated into **kSuite**, particularly within **kChat**. It acts as a conversational agent to assist you with various tasks, such as:
- Answering questions on a wide range of topics.
- Performing calculations and translations.

- Sending welcome messages to new users automatically.

### **How to Use Euria in kChat**
#### **Prerequisites**
- You must have access to **kChat** as part of a **kSuite** organization.
- Euria is automatically available to all users in your organization once enabled by the **Administrator** or **Legal Representative**.
- New users receive a **welcome message from Euria** upon joining kChat.

#### **Platform Limitations**
- Euria is available on **all platforms** (web, desktop, and mobile apps for iOS and Android).
- Some features, like **summarizing discussions**, are only available in the **web and desktop apps** (not mobile).

#### **How to Add Euria to Your Contacts**
Euria is already part of your contacts as a **bot**. If you don’t see it:
1. Open kChat.
2. In the left sidebar:
   - Click the **search bar** (Euria appears as a channel).
   - Or click the **+** icon next to **Direct Messages** to search for Euria.
3. Search for **Euria** or **kChat Bot** (it is labeled with the tag **[bot]**).
4. Start a **private conversation** with Euria (do not create a group conversation, as it won’t work).

---

#### **How to Use Euria in kChat**
##### **1. Conversational Agent**
- Start a **private chat** with Euria.
- Ask questions or request assistance (e.g., calculations, translations, or general information).
- Example: *"Translate 'Hello' to Spanish"* or *"What is the capital of Japan?"*

##### **2. Summarize a Discussion Thread**
- Hover over a message in a **thread** or **channel**.
- Click the **Euria actions icon** (✨) in the top-right corner of the message.
- Select **Summarize the discussion thread**.
- Euria will generate a summary and display it in the **right sidebar**.

##### **3. Set Reminders for Messages**
- Hover over a message and click the **three-dot menu (•••)**.
- Select **Remind** and choose a time (e.g., "In 1 hour," "Tomorrow," or "Custom time").
- Euria will notify you at the selected time with a reminder.

---

#### **User Role Requirements**
- **All users** in the organization can interact with Euria.
- **Administrators** or **Legal Representatives** must enable Euria for the organization in **kSuite settings**.

---

#### **Important Notes**
- Euria **only has access to the content of the conversation or document you are interacting with**. It does not browse your entire kChat history or kDrive files unless explicitly opened.
- Euria’s responses are **generated by AI** and may not always be 100% accurate. Use critical thinking when relying on its answers.
- For **kDrive**, Euria only works with specific file types:
  - **PDFs**
  - Text files (`.txt`, `.md`, `.json`, `.php`, etc.).
- Euria is **not available** for **guest users** with limited permissions.

---

#### **Default Behaviors**
- New users automatically receive a **welcome message** from Euria.
- Euria is **enabled by default** for all users in the organization unless disabled by an Administrator.

---

#### **Related Actions**
- **Disable Euria**: Administrators can disable Euria in the [kSuite settings](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/all?global-settings=user-apps).
- **Revoke document access**: Users can revoke Euria’s access to document content in [kDrive settings](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2412).
- **Manage reminders**: You can cancel or modify reminders set by Euria in the notification panel.
